360-program-description: Honours training in statistics with a mathematical core and computing, focusing as you choose on probability, mathematical or applied statistics, actuarial science and finance, or data science. Can lead to the A.Stat.
360-degree-requirements-b-a-students: 60–63 credits, depending on whether you need MATH 222. See p. 151 and an Arts OASIS adviser.
360-program-prerequisites: Enter with high standing in the listed courses or equivalents; MATH 150 and 151 equal MATH 140, 141 and 222.
360-required-courses-25-28-credits: Without MATH 222's equivalent, see an adviser and take it in your first semester. With little programming, take COMP 202, 204 or 208 before COMP 250. Take MATH 203 before MATH 204. MATH 251 or 247, not both.
Honours needs a 3.00 CGPA in program math and overall. The Department assigns credit for transfers in.
361-complementary-courses-35-credits: Mathematical statistics grad school: MATH 587 and honours courses such as MATH 358, 454 and 455.
Applied statistics or industry and government careers: MATH 523, 524, 547, one of 525 or 558, and Part III courses. Ask about the A.Stat.
Lists are given for interests in probability, actuarial science, and data science and machine learning.
361-part-i: Taking both MATH 245 and MATH 254 is strongly recommended.
362-part-ii: 6–11 credits in math and computer science, plus any other 500-level course from the Department. MATH 248 or 358, not both. MATH 455 and 587 can both count.
362-part-iii: 18–23 credits: 15–23 from the main list, 0–3 with no Honours equivalent, 0–8 from the last, MATH 594 or 598 not both. MATH 204 comes before MATH 357 or 533; take MATH 203 before MATH 204.
362-program-description: An overview of the foundations of mathematics.
363-guidelines-for-course-selection: Advanced Standing removes 100-level math. A 200+ exemption without credit means a complementary instead. Honours courses can substitute, and those heading to graduate math should do so.

For computer science: MATH 317, 318, 327, 340, 417 and the CS Minor. For statistics: the Statistics Minor or Major. For applied math: MATH 317, 319, 324, 326, 327, 417. For business, industry or government: MATH 317, 319, 327, 417, 423, 447.
If you do well in MATH 242 and 235, ask about an Honours program.
363-complementary-courses-18-credits: 9–18, 0–3 and 0–9 from the three lists. MATH 249 or 316, not both.
364-program-description: Combine with another Arts discipline. Keep GPA and CGPA 3.00 in Mathematics, and change program before final year if you're struggling.
364-complementary-courses-27-credits: 3 from each of two lists (MATH 254 and MATH 358 strongly recommended), 15 from the third, the rest from Honours courses.
364-program-description-2: Honours training in discrete or continuous applied math: numerical analysis, optimization, graph theory, discrete probability, and interdisciplinary research with biology and biomedical sciences. 60–63 credits.
365-program-prerequisites: High standing in the listed courses. Without MATH 222's equivalent, see an adviser and take it first. COMP 202 or equivalent is a prerequisite. Honours needs CGPA 3.00 in program math and overall.
365-required-courses-3639-credits: Weak programmers take COMP 202, 204 or 208 before COMP 250. MATH 222 isn't needed after MATH 150 and 151. MATH 251 or 247, not both.
365-complementary-courses-24-credits: 3 from each of four pairs (MATH 245 and 254 strongly recommended), 0–6 with no Honours equivalent, 0–12 from the list and all 500-level MATH; others with permission.
366-program-description: Honours training for analysis, number theory, geometry, geometric group theory and probability. 60–63 credits.
366-program-prerequisites: High standing in the listed courses. Without MATH 222's equivalent, see an adviser and take it first. Honours needs CGPA 3.00 in program math and overall.
367-required-courses-45-credits: MATH 222 isn't needed after MATH 150 and 151 or an equivalent.
367-complementary-courses-15-credits: 3 each from two pairs (MATH 245 and 254 strongly recommended), 0–6 with no Honours equivalent, 6–12 from the list and all 500-level MATH; others with permission. Weak programmers take COMP 202, 204 or 208 before COMP 250.
367-program-description: Rigorous honours training in both fields and how they interact. 72–78 credits.
368-program-prerequisites: See an Honours adviser in both departments. Honours needs CGPA 3.00 in program math and overall.
368-required-courses-33-36-credits: MATH 222 isn't needed after MATH 150 and 151 or an equivalent.
368-complementary-courses-39-42-credits: 0–3 programming (skip if you know it), 3 each from three pairs (MATH 245 and 254 recommended), 9–18 from the list, 0–9 honours or 500-level math, and 12 COMP at 300+ (not COMP 396), or ECSE 508.
369-mcgill-writing-centre: Courses in academic writing and communication, ESL and academic English, all now under WCOM (formerly CCOM, ESLN, CESL, EAPR, CEAP). Some are approved for the BA Foundation Program.
Up to 12 credits of WCOM ESL if English isn't your primary language and you've had under five years of English secondary school. Placement tests apply.
369-about-the-mcgill-writing-centre: In the McLennan-Redpath Library. Credit courses in academic, science, creative, digital and professional communication, a tutorial service for students, and non-credit courses open to the public.
369-mcgill-writing-centre-faculty: Director: Yvonne Hung. Academic staff: Mehdi Babaei, Donetta Hines, Kyle Kubler, Ross Sundberg.
369-academic-skills-and-communication: For English language learners; placement test required.
369-business-communication: Required for some SCS certificates; others ask the Centre.
369-location: McLennan-Redpath Library, Main Floor, Room 2, 3459 McTavish St.
370-music-minor-programs-approved-by-fac: See Arts OASIS for approved minors.
370-music-elective-courses-offered-by-th: B.A. students may take music courses, including MUEN ensembles, with prerequisites or the instructor's approval.
370-location: Strathcona Music Building, 555 Sherbrooke St. W.
371-about-philosophy: Understanding ourselves, the world and our place in it. Epistemology, metaphysics, ethics, political philosophy, logic, and the philosophies of science, language, mind and religion, plus the history of philosophy. Stresses clarity, rigour and intellectual generosity.
Honours and Joint Honours students take PHIL 301, closed to others. The B.A. isn't a professional qualification, but prepares you for graduate work and other fields like law.
371-about-history-and-philosophy-of-scie: Science through its historical development and philosophical principles. Independent research courses can count.
371-minor-in-cognitive-science: An option for those interested in cognition (p. 1165).
371-location: Leacock Building, 9th Floor, 855 Sherbrooke St. W.
371-program-description-complementary-co: At most 9 at 200, at least 3 at 400–500. 15 from Groups A–E, with at least four groups covered; 3 more from those or other PHIL.
372-program-description: Science through its historical development and philosophical principles.
373-complementary-courses-33-credits: At most 9 at 200, at least 9 at 400–500. 3 from A, 3 from B, 6 from C or D, 3 from E, 3 from F, plus 15 more. Only one of PHIL 200 or 201.
374-program-description: Enter with CGPA 3.00 and GPA 3.00 in Philosophy, and keep both.
374-complementary-courses-45-credits: 3, 3, 6, 6 and 3 from the five lists; 24 more PHIL with 12 at 400–500 (not PHIL 499), 3 at 500. At most 15 at 200, and only one of PHIL 200 or 201.
375-program-description: Combine with another Arts discipline, with course approval in each first. Enter with CGPA 3.00 and GPA 3.00 in Philosophy, and keep both.
376-group-b: 6 from A or B, 3 from the list, 9 PHIL at 400–500 (not the tutorial), 3 at 500.
376-joint-honours-tutorial-with-thesis: 3 credits: a 6-credit interdisciplinary thesis or a 3-credit thesis in PHIL 498.
377-about-political-science: See a departmental adviser each year to plan and graduate on time.
377-procedure-for-new-students: Read the Programs Guide, then attend the information meeting at the end of August in Montréal before seeing an adviser.
377-for-all-political-science-students: The Programs Guide is on the website. To count courses from elsewhere, bring transcripts and syllabi to the Director. Honours starts in your second year, except Joint Honours. Check updates at the office.
377-location: Leacock Building, 4th Floor, 855 Sherbrooke St. W.
377-program-description: Comparative politics, international relations, Canadian politics, political theory, and empirical methods.
377-complementary-courses-18-credits: 6 or 9 POLI at 200, each in a different group; the rest at 300–400, needing a 200-level course in that field. At most 6 transfer. POLI 490 and 499 aren't open.
379-program-description: Comparative politics, international relations, Canadian politics, political theory, and empirical methods.
379-complementary-courses-36-credits: POLI at 200+. At most 18 in one field (21 for Comparative). 12 at 200, at most 3 per group; the other 24 at 300–400, with 3 at 400 taken at McGill (not POLI 599).
Each 300–400 course needs a 200-level one in that field, so finish 200 in two years. At most 12 transfer, and no outside equivalents for Methods.
